title: Taiwan’s New F-16s: Why They Still Matter
gist: The first two of 66 F-16C/D Block 70 jets ordered by Taiwan's air force have arrived after years of production delays and a request history spanning the Bush, Obama and first Trump administrations. Their arrival revives debate over whether Taiwan's vulnerable air bases could sustain fighter operations in wartime.

insights.claim: The first pair of the 66 F-16C/D Block 70 aircraft ordered by the Republic of China Air Force (Taiwan) have arrived, after production delays.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Delivery start of a long-delayed Lockheed Martin backlog order; pace of remaining deliveries is a gauge of US defense-industrial capacity and Taiwan's air defense readiness.
insights.quote: The arrival of the first pair of the 66 F-16C/D Block 70 aircraft on order to the Republic of China Air Force (ROCAF) has been a long time coming
insights.locator: The arrival of the first pair

insights.claim: Taiwan first sought 66 F-16C/Ds under President George W. Bush; the request was blocked by his administration, remained unapproved under Barack Obama, and was only signed off in 2019 during Donald Trump's first term.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Shows US arms sales to Taiwan have historically been subject to China-sensitivity calculations across administrations, with Trump's first term more willing to approve major platforms.

themes.theme: Survivability of fighters in a Taiwan conflict

insights.claim: The new F-16s arrive after years of debate over whether Taiwan's vulnerable air bases could sustain fighter operations in wartime, raising questions over what role the aircraft can realistically play.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Base vulnerability to Chinese missile strikes favors spending on asymmetric capabilities, hardening and dispersal over expensive manned fighters — relevant to the mix of future Taiwan defense procurement.
insights.quote: their arrival comes after years of debate over whether Taiwan’s vulnerable air bases could sustain fighter operations in wartime
insights.locator: Yet their arrival comes after years

insights.claim: The author's framing ('Why They Still Matter') implies he believes the F-16s retain meaningful value for Taiwan despite air-base vulnerability concerns.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Pushes back on the asymmetric-only school of Taiwan defense, supporting continued demand for conventional platforms.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s New F-16s: Why They Still Matter

themes.theme: Historical origins of Taiwan's fighter procurement

insights.claim: In the 1970s Taiwan's F-100 and F-104 fleet was heading toward obsolescence; Washington and Taipei agreed to co-produce the upgraded F-5E/F, but many U.S. officials saw additional F-5Es as inadequate long term.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Taiwan's capability gaps have repeatedly been filled with second-best options due to political constraints, a pattern that persists.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s F-16 story begins in the 1970s

insights.claim: US-mainland China reconciliation in the 1970s complicated any follow-on fighter agreements with Taiwan, illustrating how US-China rapprochement constrains arms supply to Taipei.
insights.speaker: Rowan Allport
insights.so_what: Periods of US-China détente historically correlate with slower or blocked Taiwan arms sales — a dynamic worth watching amid current summit diplomacy.
insights.quote: Complicating any follow-on agreements, however, was the steady reconciliation between the U.S. and mainland China.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s F-16 story begins in the 1970s
